question: What proportion of significant caQTL lead SNPs lie within 1,000 bp of their peak center? Choose from these approximate options: 20%, 50%, 75%, or 100%.

nodes.label: Clarify input data structures for caQTL lead SNPs and ATAC peak coordinates, ensuring both are on the same genome build and in comparable formats
Define the distance metric as the absolute genomic distance between each lead SNP position and the center of its associated consensus ATAC peak
Compute the absolute distance from each significant caQTL lead SNP to its peak center and obtain the empirical distribution of these distances
Calculate the proportion of lead SNPs with distance ≤ 1,000 bp from their peak center across all significant caQTLs
Compare the estimated proportion to the candidate values (20%, 50%, 75%, 100%) and choose the closest biologically plausible option given typical caQTL geometry
Load significant caQTL lead SNP table and consensus ATAC peak BED file, confirming shared genome build, chromosome naming, and coordinate system
For each consensus ATAC peak, compute the peak center as center = floor((start + end) / 2) and define the SNP–peak distance as abs(snp_pos - center)
Join each significant caQTL lead SNP to its associated consensus ATAC peak, compute abs(snp_pos - peak_center) for all pairs, and save the resulting distance vector
Compute the proportion of significant caQTL lead SNPs whose distance to their peak center is less than or equal to 1000 bp by calculating mean(distance <= 1000)
Compare the computed proportion to 0.20, 0.50, 0.75, and 1.00, choose the closest value, and verify that it is consistent with known caQTL distance enrichments near peak centers
